findings.title: Escaping-path validation throws the wrong error class and has no direct negative test
findings.detail: assertFactoryGitHubPublicationRequest calls assertFactoryGitPath (git-objects.ts) unguarded at four call sites: file.path (193), each protectedPaths entry (210), each allowedPaths entry (211), dependencyLockPath (212). assertFactoryGitPath throws FactoryGitObjectError('factory_git_path_invalid') for a leading '/', a backslash, a control character, or a '.'/'..'/'.git' path segment (git-objects.ts:75-79) -- exactly the escaping-path shape the plan requires rejected. The normalizing try/catch at release-github.ts:216-227, which converts FactoryGitObjectError into this module's own FactoryGitHubError vocabulary, wraps only the base/tree/commit SHA identity checks (217-222), not these four calls. Verified against releases.ts's dispatch(), pre-existing and unmodified by this package (confirmed via git log -L over that range against integ/w00..HEAD): its bare catch converts ANY thrown error, including a raw FactoryGitObjectError, into state uncertain/provider_response_unknown. Practical effect: the request is still rejected before any network call -- this.plan(claim) runs before the first this.call(...) in publish() -- so it fails closed and is not a security defect, but it lands as an ambiguous 'uncertain' operation needing operator reconciliation instead of a clean typed rejection. No test in release-github.test.ts submits an actual escaping path (e.g. '../x', an absolute path, a '.git/...' segment) through files[].path, protectedPaths, allowedPaths, or dependencyLockPath; the existing 'escaping links' case only varies symlink content under mode 120000, which is rejected unconditionally regardless of content and never reaches this code path.
findings.recommendation: Widen the try/catch in assertFactoryGitHubPublicationRequest to cover the four assertFactoryGitPath call sites, and add a negative test submitting an actual escaping path in each of the four locations, asserting a typed FactoryGitHubError and zero network calls.
